metadata.name: Measure Forest Change
metadata.description:
## Introduction
The Measure Forest Change pipeline maps forest loss, forest gain, and areas with no detected change using [Global Forest Watch (GFW)](https://globalnaturewatch.org/) data. It uses tree-cover percentage in 2000 as the forest baseline, applies a user-defined minimum tree-cover threshold for each of Guinea's four natural regions, and removes forest loss recorded before the selected initial year to create a baseline for the analysis period. The pipeline then combines this baseline with forest-loss and forest-gain layers to classify each mapped pixel as no change, loss, or gain.

You can analyze all of Guinea or focus on a smaller area. The pipeline reports results for Forest Guinea, Maritime Guinea, Middle Guinea, and Upper Guinea wherever they overlap the selected area. [View all four regions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6ccac41-c645-4de0-88a1-ef24a94a6c8a).
## Uses
Use the pipeline to see where forest change was detected, compare forest loss across regions, and summarize the area affected in hectares. These results can support forest monitoring, conservation planning, and reporting.
## Pipeline limitations
* **Geographic coverage.** The pipeline uses fixed boundaries for Guinea’s four natural regions. A custom analysis area limits which parts of those regions are included.
* **What tree-cover loss measures**. GFW detects canopy removal. The loss layer alone cannot distinguish permanent deforestation from harvesting, fire, or other disturbances.
* **Timing of forest gain.** The selected years define the forest-loss analysis. Forest gain comes from the GFW gain layer’s fixed source period (2000 - 2012).
* **Source data detail.** The resolution and classification accuracy of the source data limit how reliably small or fragmented changes can be detected.
## Before you start
For all of Guinea, choose Country or region, select Guinea, and leave the area file blank. To focus on a smaller area, draw a bounding box or choose Polygon or Raster and provide the matching file. A polygon clips the analysis to its boundary. A raster defines a rectangular extent.

Choose a start year of 2000 or later and an end year after the start year, up to 2020. The year 2000 is the earliest baseline year, and annual loss observations begin in 2001.

View the [GEO BON STAC catalog](https://stac.geobon.org/) to inspect the GFW tree-cover and loss-year collections used by the pipeline.
